hook.line: At the door of the cooperative's meeting room there is a sign. Notices rarely say who is asking, they just ask.
hook.es: Se ruega no fumar en las instalaciones.
hook.en: Please refrain from smoking on the premises.

examples.es: Se ruega no fumar en las instalaciones.
examples.en: Please refrain from smoking on the premises.

examples.es: Se ruega a los asistentes que apaguen el celular.
examples.en: Attendees are asked to switch off their phones.

examples.es: Se ruega no dejar bolsas en la entrada.
examples.en: Please do not leave bags at the entrance.

examples.en: Customers are asked to pay at the register.

examples.es: Se ruega silencio durante la reunión.
examples.en: Silence is requested during the meeting.

rule:
*Se ruega* is a polite request from nobody in particular.

*Se ruega* + infinitive: *Se ruega no fumar.*
*Se ruega* + noun: *Se ruega puntualidad.*
*Se ruega a* + who + *que* + a changed verb: *Se ruega a los asistentes que apaguen el celular.*

The verb after *que* takes the *-en* / *-e* ending (*apaguen*, *lleguen*), not the usual one. English says *please* or *kindly*. Spanish keeps the sentence impersonal.
smallPrint: Teachers call this an impersonal *se* request, with the subjunctive after *que*.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *a* or *de*, then type the whole sentence: Se ruega ___ los asistentes que apaguen el celular. (Attendees are asked to switch off their phones.)
yourTurn.answer: Se ruega a los asistentes que apaguen el celular.
yourTurn.why: The people being asked come after *a*.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *lleguen* or *llegan*, then type the whole sentence: Se ruega a los asistentes que ___ temprano. (arrive early)
yourTurn.answer: Se ruega a los asistentes que lleguen temprano.
yourTurn.why: After *se ruega que* the verb takes the changed ending: *lleguen*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type it in Spanish: Please do not use your phone during the meeting. (a notice)
yourTurn.answer: Se ruega no usar el celular durante la junta.
yourTurn.why: *Se ruega no* + infinitive makes a notice.

yourTurn.prompt: Type it in Spanish: Customers are asked to pay at the register.
yourTurn.answer: Se ruega a los clientes que paguen en la caja.
yourTurn.why: Who is asked goes after *a*, then *que* and the changed verb.

yourTurn.prompt: Type it in Spanish: Silence is requested during the meeting.
yourTurn.answer: Se ruega silencio durante la reunión.
yourTurn.why: *Se ruega* can take a noun directly.

yourTurn.prompt: Type it in Spanish: Please reply before Friday. (a notice)
yourTurn.answer: Se ruega responder antes del viernes.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it negative: Se ruega dejar bolsas en la entrada.
yourTurn.answer: Se ruega no dejar bolsas en la entrada.

pitfalls.wrong: Se ruega a los asistentes apaguen el celular.
pitfalls.right: Se ruega a los asistentes que apaguen el celular.
pitfalls.why: Almost. When you name who is asked, *que* has to introduce the request.

pitfalls.wrong: Se ruega no fuman en las instalaciones.
pitfalls.right: Se ruega no fumar en las instalaciones.
pitfalls.why: Almost. After *se ruega no*, the verb stays an infinitive.

pitfalls.wrong: Se ruega a los asistentes que apagan el celular.
pitfalls.right: Se ruega a los asistentes que apaguen el celular.
pitfalls.why: Almost. After *que* in a request, the verb takes the changed ending: *apaguen*.

personal: Imagine a sign for your own home or office, and write it with *Se ruega*.
